goals: Mechanistic: quantify how elevation controls snowmelt-onset day-of-year across the Naches
Validation: reproduce observed SWE magnitude and melt timing at the 6 Naches SNOTEL stations
Sub-goal (flagged infeasible): resolve the local temperature lapse rate between same-ridge stations <12 km apart

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates snowpack (H2OSNO/SWE, QSNOMELT) in default output, enabling co-located comparison to SNOTEL SWE and derivation of melt-onset DOY.

answerable: Co-located SWE / melt-timing validation at each SNOTEL station (SWE is in default history output)
Basin-SCALE elevation control on melt DOY, to the extent stations/columns fall in DIFFERENT 12 km NLDAS cells (which carry some orographic precip/temperature variation)

not_answerable.aspect: Local lapse rate between same-ridge SNOTEL stations <12 km apart
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 forcing is ~12 km with no within-cell lapse rate; stations closer than the cell size share identical forcing, so ELM cannot generate an elevation-driven temperature difference between them
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled (sub-12 km) forcing with within-cell lapse-rate correction

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 6 validation columns are fixed by the 6 SNOTEL stations. 5 exploratory columns span the 352-1977 m gradient in ~3 elevation bands, concentrated in the rain-snow transition where melt-onset DOY is most sensitive, to characterize the COARSE (cross-cell) elevation signal the forcing CAN resolve. Kept small because the fine-scale lapse-rate question is infeasible and denser sampling within a 12 km cell adds no forcing contrast.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Pin 6 columns at SNOTEL sites for validation; place exploratory columns to maximize the number of DISTINCT 12 km NLDAS cells sampled across the elevation range, biased toward the 900-1400 m rain-snow transition where melt timing swings most.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — replicate columns within a single 12 km cell would see identical forcing and add no information.

sampling_plan.reason: One column pinned at each of the 6 Naches SNOTEL stations for co-located SWE and melt-timing validation.
Anchor the warm/ephemeral-snow end of the elevation gradient for the coarse elevation-vs-melt-DOY relationship.
Oversample the transition band where melt-onset DOY is most sensitive to elevation, using distinct NLDAS cells.
Anchor the cold/deep-snowpack end of the gradient; also documents expected ridgetop SWE underestimation from 12 km averaging.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — column placed at each station cell; compare modeled H2OSNO/QSNOMELT-derived melt-onset DOY and peak SWE to station record
validation_design.metric: DOY bias (days) for melt onset; bias/RMSE for peak SWE

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 default forcing (nearest 12 km cell), native SSURGO soil, one antecedent autumn to initialize snowpack (snow is a fast state; no multi-year spin-up needed)

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled (sub-12 km) forcing with within-cell lapse-rate correction
requires_capabilities.why: SNOTEL stations <12 km apart share one NLDAS cell and identical forcing
requires_capabilities.blocks: resolving the LOCAL lapse rate / between-station melt-DOY differences on the same ridge — the user's primary sub-goal

requires_capabilities.why: brief gives station count but no lat/lon; validation columns must be pinned to true station locations
requires_capabilities.blocks: concrete placement of the 6 validation columns

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM / elevation sampling within the HUC
requires_capabilities.why: exploratory columns must be placed by elevation band and their elevations known
requires_capabilities.blocks: concrete placement and elevation labeling of exploratory columns

requires_capabilities.capability: melt-onset DOY extraction from SWE/QSNOMELT time series
requires_capabilities.why: melt onset must be defined consistently (e.g. first sustained QSNOMELT after peak SWE) for model-vs-SNOTEL comparison

assumptions: SNOTEL SWE records overlap the 1980-2018 forcing window for at least several water years.
Snowmelt onset can be operationally defined from peak-SWE decline / sustained QSNOMELT.
A single antecedent autumn adequately initializes the snowpack (no deep-state spin-up required for snow).
open_questions: What are the 6 SNOTEL station coordinates and elevations, and which pairs are <12 km apart (i.e. share an NLDAS cell)?
Which water years should be analyzed — a representative subset or the full 1980-2018 climatology of melt DOY?
Is a coarse basin-scale elevation-vs-melt-DOY relationship an acceptable partial answer given the local lapse-rate goal is not resolvable with current forcing?
